verifications.claim: id: PAT_COLE; nameMain: Cole; nameSystem: hereditary_family_name; transmissionMode: patrilineal; designatedSocialUnit: other

candidates.title: Elite persistence in Sierra Leone: what can names tell us? (African Economic History Working Paper No. 71)
candidates.author: Yannick Dupraz, Rebecca Simson
candidates.quote: Most held or assumed a set of common Anglo-Saxon last names associated with the first settlers from the Americas or with British administrators and settlers, such as Cole, Davies, Johnson and Williams.
candidates.supports: Cole is a hereditary family name in Sierra Leone, held by Krio families and associated with settlers and British administrators. Working paper, not peer reviewed (the paper says so itself). Read in full text on 2026-11-08. The passage does not state the transmission rule.

verifications.claim: id: PAT_COKER; nameMain: Coker; nameSystem: hereditary_family_name; transmissionMode: patrilineal; designatedSocialUnit: other

candidates.title: Elite persistence in Sierra Leone: what can names tell us? (African Economic History Working Paper No. 71)
candidates.author: Yannick Dupraz, Rebecca Simson
candidates.quote: Some of the most common Krio surnames are names of known European settlers (Cole, Coker).
candidates.supports: Coker is a hereditary family name among the Krio of Sierra Leone, of settler origin. Working paper, not peer reviewed. Read in full text on 2026-11-08. The passage does not state the transmission rule.

candidates.title: Marcelino Marques de Barros an Hugo Schuchardt (03-00537), Lisbon, 5 July 1885
candidates.author: Marcelino Marques de Barros
candidates.quote: somente Cól po Có, tribu papel com este appelido
candidates.supports: Có is a surname borne by a group of the Papel (Guinea-Bissau), per a nineteenth-century correspondent. Hugo Schuchardt Archiv, ed. Silvio Moreira de Sousa (2015). The page was read through a summarising fetch tool, so the quote should be checked against the live page. A primary letter, not a study of the name.
